stem: Explain the immediate origin of pressure exerted by a gas on its container.

options.A: The weight of all molecules alone
options.B: Molecular collisions with the container wall
options.D: Attraction between molecules and the wall

stem: State what each molecular collision with a rigid wall transfers to the wall.

Explain why gas pressure acts on the side walls of a sealed vessel.

options.B: Moving molecules collide with every wall
options.D: Only molecule–molecule collisions act on walls

stem: Identify the quantity that directly determines pressure at a given wall area.
Describe what happens to a molecule when it rebounds from a container wall.

options.B: Its momentum changes and the wall experiences a force

stem: State the two defining ideal-gas particle assumptions.

options.A: Finite particle volume and strong attractions
options.B: Zero particle volume and no intermolecular attraction
options.C: Zero particle mass and no collisions
options.D: No molecular motion and no collisions

stem: Identify what is treated as zero for an ideal gas molecule.

Explain why a gas with stronger attractions departs more from ideal behaviour.

options.B: Its molecules exert intermolecular forces absent from the ideal model
